land.text: Kuntala: north Karnataka and south Maharashtra, taken from the Vakataka shape

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws 451 of the Kadamba shape's 810 cells out of the Vakataka shape in 353; the Vakataka pages say Vindhyasena (c. 355-400) conquered Kuntala. The Kadamba page has Mayurasharma subduing local rulers and defeating the Pallava armies.

land.text: the Kadamba lands that Cliopatria's Chalukya shape of 555 covers

successors.note: Kadamba page: 'Around c. 540 the Chalukyas who were vassals of the Kadambas and governed from Badami conquered the entire kingdom.' Cliopatria's Chalukya row starts 555 and covers 436 of the last Kadamba shape's 813 cells.

capitals.name: Banavasi
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Banavasi'; Banavasi was 'the nerve center of power' while Halasi, Triparvata and Uchangi were important regional capitals; the Triparvata branch (from c. 455) ruled from Devagiri (Dharwad district) or Halebidu.

correction.text: Banavasi in Uttara Kannada and its country, the Kadamba seat on the Varada

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 345-352: infobox 'Established: 345' and 'The kingdom was founded by Mayurasharma in c. 345', but Cliopatria's first Kadamba shape starts in 353 at 201,491 km2. The conquests that fill that shape (the Brihad-Banas of Kolar, Traikutas, Abhiras, Pariyathrakas, Shakasthanas, Maukharis) are undated within Mayurasharma's reign (345-365), so only the Banavasi core is drawn for 345-352; the 353 shape follows.

201,492 km2 (810 cells): Karnataka 69%, southern Maharashtra 18%, Kurnool edge. The page: the Kadambas 'ruled northern Karnataka and the Konkan from Banavasi'; Mayurasharma subdued the 'Traikutas, the Abhiras, the Pariyathrakas, the Shakasthanas, the Maukharis'; the Mayurasharma page has the Pallavas under Skandavarman 'recognised him as a sovereign in the regions from the Amara ocean (western ocean) to Prehara' (the Malaprabha). The shape covers that block. 451 of its cells are Cliopatria's Vakataka land; the Vakataka pages call Kuntala Vakataka (Vindhyasena, c. 355-400): contested, kept as drawn. The page gives no area.

Years only: the shape holds 451-540. 202,263 km2 (+5/-2 cells on 353). Kakusthavarma's reign is the peak ('The Kadamba power reached its peak during the rule of Kakusthavarma'), with daughters married to the Guptas, the Gangas and the Vakataka prince Narendrasena; Santivarma divided the kingdom c. 455 (the Triparvata branch under Krishnavarma), Ravivarma 'was able to build the kingdom back to its original might' (to c. 519), Sircar thinks his suzerainty reached 'the whole of South India', which the shape does not draw; Krishnavarma II reunited the branches c. 530.

correction.text: years do not belong to the Kadamba state: the kingdom ends c. 540 and the Chalukyas of Badami hold it

keyframe_review.note: The shape belongs to no year of the Kadamba state: infobox 'Disestablished: 540' and 'Around c. 540 the Chalukyas who were vassals of the Kadambas and governed from Badami conquered the entire kingdom.' Cliopatria keeps the row to 554 and starts the Chalukya row in 555 over only 436 of its 813 cells (a Chalukya group, sa-03, should consider an earlier start). For 541-554 use the successor.

region.text: Banavasi in Uttara Kannada and its country, the Kadamba seat on the Varada

ledger.note: c. 345: Mayurasharma founds the Kadamba kingdom at Banavasi. 'The kingdom was founded by Mayurasharma in c. 345'; he went to Kanchi, quarrelled with a Pallava guard and left 'swearing vengeance on the Pallavas'; 'Mayurasharma defeated the armies of the Pallavas of Kanchi'; the Mayurasharma page: he established a capital at Banavasi. The Banavasi radius is the researcher's reading; the page gives no frontier for the first years.

region.text: Kuntala: north Karnataka and south Maharashtra

ledger.note: c. 353: the Kadamba shape takes Kuntala from the Vakataka shape (451 cells). Kadamba page: Kangavarma (c. 365) 'had to fight the Vakataka might to protect his kingdom'; Bhageerath (c. 390) is described as retrieving his father's losses, though the Vakataka inscriptions do not confirm this. The Prithivishena I page: Vindhyasena conquered Kuntala, so the main branch were 'lords of Kuntala'. Year is Cliopatria's.

minus.text: Banavasi in Uttara Kannada and its country, the Kadamba seat on the Varada

region.text: the Karnataka coast, the Konkan edge and the Kolar country, outside the Banavasi core and the Vakataka shape

ledger.note: c. 353: the rest of Mayurasharma's conquests (about 270 cells outside the Banavasi core). He 'subdued the Traikutas, the Abhiras, the Pariyathrakas, the Shakasthanas, the Maukharis' and the Brihad-Banas of Kolar; the Mayurasharma page adds the Sendrakas and Punnatas and the Pallava recognition of his sovereignty from the western ocean to the Malaprabha. Undated within his reign (345-365); the year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: the Kadamba shape: northern Karnataka and the Konkan around Banavasi

ledger.note: c. 540: the Chalukyas of Badami, the Kadambas' own vassals, conquer the kingdom. Infobox 'Disestablished: 540'; 'Around c. 540 the Chalukyas who were vassals of the Kadambas and governed from Badami conquered the entire kingdom.' The Kadamba page does not name Kirtivarman I or give a later date; Cliopatria runs the shape to 554.

wars.name: Mayurasharma's revolt against the Pallavas
wars.outcome: Mayurasharma defeated the Pallava armies, subdued neighbouring tribes and was recognised as sovereign by the Pallava king Skandavarman from the western ocean to the Malaprabha.
wars.note: The page puts his early base at Shriparvata, 'possibly modern Srisailam' (Mayurasharma page); no border is dated.

wars.name: Kangavarma's war with the Vakatakas
wars.outcome: Kangavarma 'had to fight the Vakataka might to protect his kingdom'; no result is given.
wars.note: Zones not drawn: no page says where the front lay; see the vakataka-kingdom notes on Kuntala.

wars.name: Raghu's war with the Pallavas
wars.outcome: Raghu 'died fighting the Pallavas in c. 435'.

wars.name: Ravivarma's war with the Vakatakas
wars.outcome: Ravivarma is credited with 'a victory against the Vakatakas' and a suzerainty over the Punnatas, Alupas, Kongalvas and the Pandyas of Uchangi.
wars.note: The Vakataka dynasty page adds that the Kadambas probably took Vakataka lands after 500.

wars.name: Krishnavarma II's reunification of the Kadambas
wars.outcome: Harivarma (c. 519) was killed around 530 by Krishnavarma II, who 'raided Banavasi and reunited the branches.

wars.name: Chalukya conquest of the Kadambas

zones.text: the Kadamba lands covered by the Chalukya shape of 555

wars.outcome: The Chalukyas, vassals of the Kadambas at Badami, conquered the entire kingdom c. 540.

certainty.note: The pages name regions (Banavasi, the Konkan, the Malaprabha) and no frontier line; the Kuntala border with the Vakataka and the southern border with the Gangas are the least certain.

notes:
Cliopatria row: one row 353-554; the dossier starts the state in 345 (infobox) and ends it c. 540 (infobox and 'Around c. 540 the Chalukyas ... conquered the entire kingdom'): 546-554 marked wrong, the 451 shape given years 451-540. Cliopatria's Chalukya row starts 555, so 541-554 leave Kadamba land to a state not yet drawn; the Chalukya dossier (sa-03) should consider an earlier start.
Page budget: 2 of 2 (Kadamba dynasty, Mayurasharma). The wikipedia field gives the article title 'Kadamba dynasty'; Cliopatria's field says 'Kadamba Empire' (a redirect).
Unsettled: (1) the Kuntala frontier with the Vakatakas (Vindhyasena c. 355-400 conquered Kuntala on the Vakataka pages; the Kadamba page has Kangavarma c. 365 fighting the Vakataka); no contest is drawn; (2) the Triparvata branch (c. 455-530) and Krishnavarma II's reunion are not split/merge events: the Cliopatria row is one state; (3) the pages differ on the Talagunda inscription (450 or c. 455), and on whether Mayurasharma's war with the Pallavas was at Kanchi, Srisailam or Palasika; (4) Ravivarma's reach (the Punnatas, Alupas, Kongalvas, Pandyas of Uchangi; Sircar's 'whole of South India') is not drawn; (5) the Kadamba page gives no ruler list with end years, so no ruler strip is written.
Gazetteer names needed: Banavasi (place, 14.53N 74.88E), Kuntala (region: north Karnataka and south Maharashtra), Halasi, Uchangi, Triparvata.
